geometry.polygon: vertical column on single-foot base; raised-leg T-branch at hip; optional overhead arm triangle
geometry.summary: Stand on one foot with the other foot pressed to the inner thigh or calf (never the knee). Keep the pelvis square and level, spine lengthening as a vertical column, and arms either at the heart or reaching up. The shape is a rooted trunk with one branch open to the side.
geometry.svg_hint: upright stick on one circle foot; second foot mid-inner thigh; arms up or anjali

reaction.name: Root settle
reaction.summary: School metaphor: wobble and chase settle into one quiet plumb line from standing sole through crown. Not a medical or biochemical claim.

breath.lands_in: standing foot sole, then low belly
breath.cue: Even breath. Soften the jaw. Let each exhale drop weight into the standing foot without collapsing the tall spine.

orientation.cue: Crown over standing heel; pelvis square to the front; raised knee opens only as far as the pelvis stays level
orientation.gravity: Whole body weight through one foot's three points (big-toe mound, little-toe mound, heel); lifted foot presses in, standing thigh presses back
orientation.gaze: Soft fixed point ahead at eye height (drishti); avoid looking down at the foot
orientation.degrees_hint: 0 deg twist; raised thigh opens in the frontal plane only while pelvis stays forward-facing

attention.primary: standing foot sole and inner standing thigh
attention.secondary: quiet vertical line sole to crown

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Utter a praṇava (such as Oṃ, or another seed sound in that family) in a drawn-out form; at the end of that protracted sound, rest attention in the silent open void. Through that spacious openness, awareness meets its own clear nature.
adiyogi.method_summary: Safe class form: after settling in Tree, silently lengthen one soft Oṃ (or simply feel the breath as sound fading). At the moment sound or breath-sound ends, rest in the quiet gap—no chasing the next thought. Keep eyes soft on the balance point; do not force breath retention.

honesty.disclosure: This asana↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. Tree and VBT 016 share a modern school rhyme (rooted body, open sky of attention), not a historical one-to-one pairing.
honesty.notes: Serial index pairing D-016 ↔ VBT dharana/yukti 016 (commonly mapped to verse 39: praṇava → śūnya at pluta-end). Experiential rhyme noted; claim kept at school_device.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: Foot to calf or toes to floor; stand near a wall; or keep both feet down in Mountain with arms branching up.
safety.contraindication_notes: Avoid pressing the raised foot into the standing knee joint. Use wall or lower foot placement if balance is unstable. General practice caution only; not medical advice.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 016: Tree, Vrksasana. One standing root, one open branch, tall spine.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: From Mountain, shift onto one foot. Place the other foot on the inner thigh or calf—never the knee. Hands at heart or reach up.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Crown over the standing heel. Keep the pelvis square. Gaze soft and fixed ahead. Wall is welcome.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Breathe four counts in, four out, about six rounds. Let the exhale land in the standing foot and low belly.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Lock attention in the standing sole and inner thigh. Feel a quiet line from foot to crown. Soften the face.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: Notice sway become a still axis. School name for that shift: Root settle. Wobble is information, not failure.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: VBT 016 thread: silently draw out a soft Om, then rest in the quiet gap when sound ends. Stay with that open silence a few breaths.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Lower the foot with control. Stand in Mountain. Switch sides when ready. Carry the quiet root into your next step.
